record.context_brief: practical algorithms from finite STFT samples
record.original_question: Can one develop practical phase-retrieval algorithms, together with window functions and finite sampling schemes in R^d x R^d, such that for every function in a dense subset of L^2(R^d) the reconstruction from finitely many sampled short-time Fourier magnitude measurements converges, up to a global phase factor, to the true function as the number of samples tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: Question 8.9. Develop practical phase retrieval algorithms A : [0, ∞)^k → L2(R^d) together with window functions w and finite sampling schemes Ωk = {(xj, ξj) | 1 ≤ j ≤ k} ⊂ R^d × R^d such that, e.g, inf_{α∈S1} ||αf − A(|Vwf|^2_{Ωk})||_{L2} → 0 as k → ∞ for all f in a dense set of functions of L2(R^d).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and a window function $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) of $f$ with respect to $w$ is defined by
$$V_w f(x,\xi) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} f(t)\,\overline{w(t-x)}\, e^{-2\pi i t\cdot \xi}\,dt, \qquad (x,\xi) \in \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d.$$
The associated spectrogram is $|V_w f|^2$. Phase retrieval seeks to reconstruct $f$ (up to a global unimodular phase factor $\alpha \in S^1 = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z|=1\}$) from magnitude measurements of $V_w f$.

Construct a window function $w \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, a sequence of finite sampling sets $\Omega_k = \{(x_j, \xi_j) : 1 \le j \le k\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d$, and a sequence of (practical, implementable) reconstruction maps
$$A_k : [0,\infty)^k \to L^2(\mathbb{R}^d),$$
such that there exists a dense subset $D \subset L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with the property that for every $f \in D$,
$$\inf_{\alpha \in S^1} \big\| \alpha f - A_k\big(|V_w f|^2 \big|_{\Omega_k}\big) \big\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)} \longrightarrow 0 \quad \text{as } k \to \infty,$$
where $|V_w f|^2|_{\Omega_k} = (|V_w f(x_j,\xi_j)|^2)_{j=1}^k$.

Either exhibit such a triple $(A_k, w, \{\Omega_k\})$ or prove that no such practical scheme exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works provide partial answers: semidefinite programming based Gabor phase retrieval with accuracy guarantees from finitely many noisy samples, provably accurate spectrogram inversion algorithms for L^2([-π,π]), and provably convergent (accelerated) Griffin–Lim type iterations. These give practical algorithms with convergence/error guarantees in restricted settings (bandlimited or smooth functions on intervals, specific windows). A fully general construction yielding convergence on a dense subset of L^2(R^d) for all d with a unified practical scheme does not appear to be established, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Phase Retrieval for L^2([-π,π]) via Provably Accurate and Noise Robust Numerical Inversion of Spectrogram Measurements
status_evidence.snippet: Two algorithms approximating smooth functions from a finite set of STFT magnitude measurements, with theoretical error guarantees and good numerical convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: provably accurate practical reconstruction from finite STFT magnitude samples in 1D bandlimited setting.

status_evidence.title: Gabor Phase Retrieval via Semidefinite Programming
status_evidence.snippet: Practical scenario with finitely many possibly noisy samples; SDP method guaranteed accurate when spectrogram is sufficiently connected.
status_evidence.claim: Provably convergent SDP-based practical Gabor phase retrieval from finitely many samples.

status_evidence.title: Accelerated Griffin–Lim algorithm: a provably converging numerical method for phase retrieval
status_evidence.snippet: Inertial/momentum-based algorithm with convergence guarantees for the Fast Griffin–Lim algorithm.
status_evidence.claim: Provides a practical, provably convergent iterative phase retrieval algorithm.
